subject: Independent source-only review of the dedicated small winning-modal Dart QA harness
result: No functional blocker found in this static request/state/reward contract review.

findings.finding: The harness imports the existing FileTransport unchanged. The observing subclass calls super.poll and records actual request objects crossing that file boundary, with adjacent duplicate polls de-duplicated.

The two required Native action records are restart then mode. All Native submitted requests must equal the independently observed requests, with an exact sequence containing two real seven-move histories and no replacement direct controller actions.

Every request is bound to a real published pre-state, exact token/round identity and production ACK. Both targeted before/after dictionaries must equal full actual publish events. Targeted pre-states are rewarded paused two-player wins; post-states must be acknowledged fresh empty active rounds, keeping two-player mode for restart and selecting solo mode for mode(false).

The second won round is linked to the first restarted round. Exact expected award IDs bind to the two won owner/round pairs; the two-player reward implementation supports exactly 10 total stars and 80 XP.

The final Native state must equal the final published state with exit ACK. The controller must retain an empty uncompleted solo round. A same-process reopen must restore that round without another award.
The report remains failed on assertion/exception, captures actual requests/events/awards in finally, and closes/disposes the isolated test session/controller resources.

production_contract_support.finding: The real session validates token, sequence, round and revision; restart/mode reset waiting time and paused state; positive ACK follows accepted action.
Restart creates a new round ID and empty history, preserves or explicitly changes mode, and the existing two-player winning reward is 5 stars/40 XP per unique owner/round.

limits: No Dart parser, analyzer, Flutter test, Godot engine or CI execution was performed for this review.
The harness explicitly uses a SharedPreferences test backend and local file transport; it is not Android Binder or a device test.
Actual scroll/input geometry and four original captures remain the separate Native overlay's responsibility; this Dart review does not claim their future execution succeeds.
No measured FPS, Android readiness or release approval is implied.
